A clear scope for body corporate repairs

We organise common-area defects by location, required work and approval, so the quotation and completion record follow the same list.

THE BRIEF

A photograph of a damaged area is a useful start. A practical work list also identifies the building element, the symptom, access and the decision needed. We use those details to separate defined repairs, investigation and proposed improvements before the work is approved.

✺

FIELD NOTES

Identify the area and the authorised brief

We begin with the nominated property representative and the work area under consideration. Building, level and item references make a public entry door, a corridor ceiling and a balcony detail distinguishable throughout the quotation and completion record.

Queensland guidance explains maintenance responsibilities through the relevant plan and boundaries. We use the scheme information and approved brief supplied for the property when defining work; we do not treat a description such as “balcony” as a complete statement of scope or responsibility.

FIELD NOTES

Make each defect useful for a decision

FieldWhat goes in itWhy it matters
Location and itemBuilding, level, door or marked surfaceLinks photos, quote and completion
Observed conditionWhat occurs, when and any previous repairSupports the investigation scope
Required actionRepair, investigate or consider an improvementKeeps different decisions separate
Access and approvalAffected areas, contact and approved boundaryMakes attendance workable
Completion statusWork done, checks, photos and remaining itemsCreates a usable property record

FIELD NOTES

Separate three different types of work

  • A defined repair

    A visible, assessed defect can be scoped with its location, method, parts and finish. The quote identifies what is included and the access required for that item.

  • Further investigation

    Recurring water or concealed damage may need a separate inspection, test or agreed opening-up scope. We record what needs to be established before a final repair can be defined.

  • A proposed improvement

    A wider finish refresh, changed layout or upgraded fitting has its own brief. We separate it from the immediate defect so the representative can review the additional work clearly.

FIELD NOTES

Group the work while retaining each location

Condition-assessment guidance for Queensland Health uses structured information about assets, condition and required work. We apply the useful recording principle to a commercial defect list: related tasks can share an attendance plan while each item retains its identity and completion status.

Repeated door hardware, paint finishes or external cleaning areas may be reviewed together. Materials, height, resident access, protection and waste still need to be defined for the relevant building areas.

FIELD NOTES

Keep access and changes controlled

  1. 01

    Confirm the representative

    We agree who provides access, coordinates notices and can approve a change to the work. Relevant site requirements are included before attendance.

  2. 02

    Define the stage

    We identify the released area, routes to remain available, the materials and the tasks to be completed within that stage.

  3. 03

    Record additional findings

    If the condition differs from the agreed scope, we document the finding and the proposed next action for the nominated decision.

FIELD NOTES

Close the loop on the same list

At completion, we match the work record to each location. Relevant photographs, actual operation or finish checks and agreed follow-up are kept with that item. A task awaiting a part or another approval stays visibly separate from a completed repair.

The result is a practical record for the next meeting, property-manager handover or maintenance visit. It also preserves the history of repeated faults, helping the next decision use the work already completed.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Should every reported defect be included as a repair in one quote?+

We first classify what is sufficiently defined, what needs investigation and what is a separate improvement. They can appear in one organised proposal while retaining their different decisions and scope.

How do you handle additional damage found during work?+

We record the location, finding and proposed work for the nominated representative. The additional scope is confirmed before it is added, with the completion record updated accordingly.
